coverage: Regional survey with selected examples; not a complete 1939 network
geometryPolicy: Straight schematic links between approximate town centers, manually placed to 0.01 degrees. Not station locations, road centerlines, surveyed alignments or evidence of service on the baseline date. Do not derive distance, crossings, capacity or travel times.

sources.title: ProRail: origins of the railways
sources.finding: Amsterdam to Haarlem opened in 1839; extensions via Leiden and The Hague reached Rotterdam between 1842 and 1847.

sources.title: Train World: Belgium on track
sources.locator: A festive start; 556 km of iron ways by 1843
sources.finding: Brussels to Mechelen opened on 5 May 1835. Brussels and Paris were connected by rail in 1846. No intermediate alignment is established here.

sources.title: Rijkswaterstaat: first motorway
sources.locator: De eerste snelweg; podcast transcript 00:00:25 to 00:00:52
sources.finding: Rijksweg 12 between Voorburg and Zoetermeer opened on 15 April 1937. The historian describes continuity of alignment at the interview location, not a surveyed geometry for this overlay.

sources.title: Network Rail: Birmingham station history
sources.finding: London to Birmingham opened in 1838.

sources.title: Network Rail: Bristol station history
sources.finding: Bristol to Bath opened in 1840, with London through traffic following in 1841.

sources.title: Dublin City: railway architecture
sources.finding: The Dublin and Kingstown passenger railway opened in December 1834. Kingstown is now Dun Laoghaire.

sources.title: City of Rouen: nineteenth century
sources.finding: Rouen was connected to Paris by rail in 1843.

sources.title: Le Havre municipal archives: economy
sources.finding: Paris to Le Havre rail opened in 1847. A carriage road between Le Havre and Rouen opened in 1769. The road evidence does not establish its 1939 standard.

sources.title: Comboios de Portugal: chronology
sources.finding: Lisbon to Carregado opened in 1856. A Lisbon to Badajoz postal train timetable was approved in September 1863. These establish connections, not modern alignment.

sources.title: Renfe: Madrid to Aranjuez history
sources.finding: Madrid to Aranjuez opened in 1851. Modern excursion train terminals must not be substituted for the original terminals.

sources.title: City of Hamburg: Lohbruegge history
sources.finding: The Hamburg to Berlin railway opened in 1846, with a station in southern Bergedorf.

sources.title: Saxon industrial heritage: Dresden Transport Museum
sources.finding: The museum account identifies the Leipzig to Dresden railway opening in 1839.

sources.title: City of Bonn: chronology
sources.finding: The grade-separated Cologne to Bonn motor road opened to traffic in 1932. Historical naming retained; modern route number not inferred.

sources.title: SBB: 175 years of Swiss railways
sources.finding: Zurich to Baden opened in 1847.

sources.title: UNESCO: Semmering Railway
sources.finding: The Gloggnitz to Muerzzuschlag mountain railway was built between 1848 and 1854. This schematic link does not locate its tunnels or viaducts.

sources.title: Fondazione FS: Bologna to Florence anniversary
sources.finding: Bologna to Florence via Prato opened in 1934. Pre-baseline electrification milestones establish other corridors: Naples to Salerno (1934), Florence to Rome to Naples (1935), Salerno to Reggio Calabria (1937), Bologna to Milan (1938). The October 1939 Chiasso milestone is excluded.

sources.title: Autostrade per Italia: Milan to Varese centenary
sources.finding: Milan to Varese motorway opened on 21 September 1924. No modern lane count is carried into the historical record.

sources.title: Bane NOR: Bergen station
sources.finding: The Bergen line entered use in 1909, four years before the present Bergen station. The page identifies the Oslo to Bergen connection.

sources.title: Trafikverket: Western Main Line centenary
sources.finding: Stockholm to Gothenburg Western Main Line was electrified in 1926. This is evidence of existence by that year, not its opening date.

sources.title: City of Helsinki: arrival of rail
sources.finding: Helsinki to Hameenlinna rail connection opened in 1862.

sources.title: Danish Railway Museum newsletter October 2019
sources.finding: Copenhagen to Roskilde opened in 1847.

sources.title: PKP: Warsaw to Vienna railway anniversary
sources.finding: Warsaw to Grodzisk opened in 1845. Rail travel from Warsaw to Krakow, Wroclaw and Vienna was possible from October 1848. Only the short opening section is plotted here.

sources.title: Czech Railways: Brandys station history
sources.finding: Prague to Olomouc was completed in 1845 and an inaugural train ran in August.

sources.title: Slovak Railways: first railways
sources.finding: Marchegg to Bratislava received a steam train in 1848. Bratislava to Sturovo to Vac was completed in 1850. The earlier horse railway is not used as a steam main line proxy.

sources.title: MAV: Pest railway origins
sources.finding: Pest to Vac opened in July 1846. Budapest is a display label, not a claim about the historical city name.

sources.title: MAV: Szolnok anniversary
sources.finding: The first train on Pest to Szolnok ran in September 1847.

sources.title: HZ Infrastruktura: Zagreb railway anniversary
sources.finding: Zidani Most to Zagreb to Sisak opened on 1 October 1862.

sources.title: Serbian transport ministry: railway anniversary
sources.finding: The first regular Belgrade to Nis train ran in 1884.

sources.title: CFR: railway history
sources.finding: Bucharest to Giurgiu opened in 1869. Pitesti to Bucharest to Galati to Roman opened in 1872.

sources.title: BDZ: railway history
sources.finding: Ruse to Varna opened in 1866; Constantinople to Belovo in 1873; Caribrod to Sofia to Belovo opened for international traffic in 1888.

sources.title: ERT archive: Athens to Piraeus
sources.finding: An archival account dates the steam connection between Piraeus and Athens (Thiseio terminus) to 1869. This is a short urban connection, not the Greek mainline network.

sources.title: Estonian Railways: history
sources.finding: Paldiski to Tallinn to Narva to Gatchina opened in 1870. Cross-border operation in 1939 is not established.

sources.title: Latvian Railways: Riga to Daugavpils
sources.finding: Riga to Daugavpils railway opened in 1861. Calendar/day differences are avoided by retaining the year only.

sources.title: Lithuanian national encyclopedia: rail transport
sources.finding: Services from St Petersburg to Vilnius and Vilnius to Virbalis began in 1862. Vilnius to Lida was built in 1884. These connections do not imply open 1939 borders.

sources.title: Russian transport ministry: railway history
sources.finding: St Petersburg to Moscow railway opened in 1851. Leningrad is the 1939 display name.

sources.title: Great Ukrainian Encyclopedia: Balta
sources.finding: The Odesa to Balta railway opened in 1865.

sources.title: Darmstaedter Tagblatt, 4 October 1935 (ULB Darmstadt)
sources.finding: The contemporary report states that the complete Frankfurt to Darmstadt to Mannheim to Heidelberg motorway was handed over to public traffic the previous Thursday. Used only for the opening report; political rhetoric and OCR errors are not treated as transport facts.

sources.title: Monitor Polski, 27 February 1933, no. 47
sources.finding: A railway directorate notice announces Herby to Gdynia service from 1 March 1933 and related timetable changes. As an advance announcement, it is paired with the PKP retrospective confirmation of opening.

sources.title: PKP: 90 years chronology
sources.finding: PKP records the coal trunk opening in 1933, Pruszkow to Warsaw to Otwock electrification in 1936, followed by Grodzisk and Zyrardow, and Minsk Mazowiecki in December 1937. These are service and upgrade observations, not opening dates for all underlying lines.

sources.title: DB Museum: Fliegender Hamburger
sources.finding: The museum records scheduled Berlin to Hamburg service from May 1933. This improves temporal evidence for the existing connection without adding a duplicate line or establishing its September 1939 operating condition.

sources.title: SNCF Heritage: Strasbourg station
sources.finding: The Paris to Strasbourg passenger line opened in July 1852.

sources.title: La Ville de Marseille, ses Finances et ses Travaux publics (period account)
sources.finding: The nineteenth-century account describes the complete main railway operating in 1856 and travel between Paris and Marseille through Lyon. This is early existence evidence, not a 1939 service record.
sources.locator: Rail transport discussion, paragraph beginning La gare de Marseille

regionPolicy: Regions are navigation groups, not 1939 states or sovereignty claims. Town names are modern navigation labels except where explicitly historical. No border crossing permission is implied.

regions.name: France and Low Countries
regions.gaps: Paris to Strasbourg and the Lyon/Marseille axis now have early existence evidence. Western and southern branches, Luxembourg and most arterial roads remain incomplete.

regions.name: Britain and Ireland
regions.gaps: Scotland, Wales, northern England and Ireland mainlines need further review. No road network yet.

regions.name: Iberia
regions.gaps: Spain and Portugal represented by a few examples. Civil War damage, border service and roads are unverified.

regions.name: Germany
regions.gaps: Berlin/Hamburg now has 1933 service evidence; the Frankfurt/Heidelberg road has a 1935 opening report. Full Reichsbahn and Autobahn coverage still needs period-map review.

regions.name: Alps
regions.gaps: Swiss and Austrian examples only; major passes and through corridors remain incomplete. Liechtenstein not reviewed.

regions.name: Italy
regions.gaps: Selected mainland trunk rail connections and one motorway. Islands, eastern corridors and most roads unrepresented.

regions.name: Nordic region
regions.gaps: Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland have examples. Northern corridors, ferries, wartime gauges and roads unreviewed; Iceland not represented.

regions.name: Poland and Carpathian region
regions.gaps: Added the coal trunk and Warsaw-area 1930s electrification evidence. Eastern Poland and most mainlines and roads remain incomplete; the 1939 map candidate has not been digitized.

regions.name: Balkans and European Turkey
regions.gaps: Romanian, Bulgarian, Yugoslav-area, Greek and European Turkish examples. Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania and much of Greece unrepresented; no road network.

regions.name: Baltic region
regions.gaps: Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian examples. Border closures, gauge history and roads need review.

regions.name: Eastern region
regions.gaps: Western Russia and Ukraine examples only. Belarus trunk network, Moldova, Caucasus and roads need further review.

mapCandidates.title: German transport and administrative map of Poland, 1939
mapCandidates.status: Catalog description reviewed; map geometry not traced
mapCandidates.finding: The catalog describes four railway classes and three road classes, based on a Polish original. Original-map public-domain status is stated; the web viewer has separate rights. Pre-invasion dating is the catalog author's inference, not a precise survey date. The Polona link currently resolves to its homepage.
mapCandidates.nextStep: Recover the exact Polona item and inspect the legend, imprint and route symbols before georeferencing.

mapCandidates.title: Central Europe and Mediterranean, Truman Library M1200
mapCandidates.status: Catalog reviewed; excluded from imported geometry
mapCandidates.finding: Catalog dates the map to circa October 1939. September 1 refers to boundaries and does not establish railway currency. The catalog identifies reproduction restrictions.
mapCandidates.nextStep: Use as a bibliographic lead; locate a suitable reusable, dated transport source before importing.
